title: Senior Engineer - Full Stack Developer
description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Hands-on design, development, deployment and lifecycle support of custom and COTS applications across the EMES scope above, used by Pharmaceutical Development within Global Product Development & Supply.
* Use Claude and GitHub Copilot as a core part of day-to-day engineering to accelerate delivery, while retaining full ownership of code quality, security, validation and maintainability.
* Build reusable AI solutions, agents and workflow automations that remove repetitive effort from the MES development and support lifecycle (code and test generation, document authoring, defect triage, validation deliverables).
* Drive AI adoption across the MES team and partner teams – run technical workshops and office hours, mentor engineers on prompting and AI best practices, and contribute to the Innovation/AI Community of Practice.
* Design, build and migrate workloads on AWS in support of cloud migration and next-generation manufacturing systems.
* Evaluate emerging AI and cloud technologies, develop proofs of concept, and measure adoption and productivity improvements against agreed metrics.
* Deliver project implementations and day-to-day operational support within a validated, GxP-regulated environment, including the associated CSV deliverables.
* Collaborate directly with business clients, IT Business Partners, site teams and other IT functions, and act as a functional mentor to more junior engineers.

**Required Qualifications & Skills**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, AI/Machine Learning or a related field, with 4-6 years of hands-on software engineering experience.
* Full stack – 4+ years building web applications using JavaScript/TypeScript with React and Node.js, plus Python for automation and AI-enabled services.
* AI-assisted engineering – demonstrable hands-on use of Claude (including Claude Code), GitHub Copilot or comparable assistants to build enterprise-grade production software, including prompt and context engineering, AI-assisted refactoring, test generation and documentation.
* AI enablement – experience building reusable AI assets (prompt libraries, agents, workflow automations, MCP-based integrations) and helping engineering teams adopt them.
* AWS – 3+ years designing and deploying solutions using services such as EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, S3, RDS, API Gateway, IAM and CloudWatch, with infrastructure-as-code and cloud migration experience.
* Strong REST API design and system-to-system integration experience, and 4+ years in RDBMS/RDS such as SQL Server including data modelling and query tuning.
* SDLC, Agile, CI/CD and source control (GIT, GitHub, Azure DevOps), with experience managing deployments of varying complexity.
* Knowledge of computer systems validation (CSV), cGxP, GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11 and data integrity requirements.
* Excellent communication, technical mentoring and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate across multiple teams.

**Good-to-Have Skills**

* Enterprise generative AI platforms (Claude for Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, custom GPTs) and building Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations to enterprise systems.
* Supporting technology adoption through training, office hours or communities of practice, including measuring adoption and productivity impact.
* Responsible AI, data privacy, information security and access management; automated testing and regression frameworks for validated systems.
* Experience in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare or another regulated industry.
* AWS Certified Develope or Microsoft/SQL Server certification(s), a plus.

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

title: Software Engineer, Data Plane / Data Path (C/Rust)
description:
**Hiring for SecurITe**
— via Flexiple, the recruiting partner on this role.

**About the Company**

SecurITe builds healthcare-native cybersecurity solutions to protect sensitive patient data, clinical systems and critical infrastructure. Its security platform combines human expertise with AI-driven intelligence, helping healthcare organizations strengthen the resilience and availability of patient care.

**About the Role**

Build high-throughput, low-latency packet-processing software for inline enforcement, out-of-band network detection and observability, and deep packet inspection. This is a hands-on systems engineering role using C or Rust.

**What you'll do**

* Build packet ingestion pipelines using DPDK and Linux capture paths such as AF\\_PACKET for bare metal and VMs.
* Implement robust L2/L3 parsing, classification and HTTP, DNS and TLS protocol handling.
* Integrate DPI pattern matching such as Hyperscan while controlling per-packet CPU and memory costs.
* Profile hotspots, cache misses, contention, allocations and copies to improve throughput and latency.
* Create unit, pcap-driven integration and performance-regression tests.
* Build metrics, tracing and packet-drop attribution to investigate loss and latency spikes.
* Define dataplane APIs, performance budgets and failure modes with policy, detection and platform engineers.

**What you bring**

* 5+ years of systems programming in C or Rust, with low-level debugging and performance-aware design.
* Experience shipping production high-throughput, low-latency packet or dataplane processing software.
* Experience implementing HTTP, DNS and TLS parsing, including real-world edge cases.
* CPU and memory profiling using benchmarks, flame graphs, contention analysis and allocator/cache investigation.
* Experience resolving packet drops, reordering, latency regressions or CPU spikes in production.
* A record of reliable tests, clear code reviews and operational documentation.

**Nice to have**

* Suricata or Snort integration and rule-performance experience.
* Linux kernel networking, NIC queues and offloads, or user-space networking.
* eBPF/XDP or other fast-I/O acceleration techniques.

title: Director, Solution Engineer, Data Storage and Registration
description: Role Summary Discovery, Preclinical, and Translational Solutions (DP&TS) sits at the center of Pfizer’s scientific software work, building the digital tools that help researchers move from target identification through clinical translation. We’re looking for a Solution Engineer to own data storage and registration for integrative biology research. This is a hands-on role: you’ll design, build, and maintain the capabilities that determine how biological research data gets stored, registered, and accessed. You’ll partner with the aligned capability lead to scope and prioritize what gets built, and work across scientific, product, and engineering stakeholders to deliver solutions that are secure, scalable, and useful for researchers. You’ll work hands-on in AWS and GCP, building storage and data services that span both clouds and hold large omics datasets (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, imaging). You’ll need depth in large-scale data management and cross-cloud integration, plus enough scientific fluency to earn credibility with computational biologists and engineers alike. Reporting to the Principal Engineer, Integrative Biology Solutions, you’ll define the technical direction for data storage and registration within the Integrative Biology space, aligning with scientific strategy, regulatory requirements, and enterprise architecture. You’re expected to be hands-on writing and reviewing real code, not just directing while also setting the standards and patterns that guide contractors and cross-functional teams. You’ll lead contractor teams as needed to extend capacity. You’re the primary technical owner: individual engineering depth combined with cross-functional leadership. The problems are real, large-scale, heterogeneous scientific data with strict regulatory requirements, and the solutions need to hold up at research scale. Key Responsibilities Own and Lead Data Storage and Registration Solutions: own data storage and registration end-to-end: design, implementation, and maintenance. Work with the Capability Lead to prioritize and scope features. Lead contractors as needed to extend capacity. Oversee Data Storage, Registration, and Scientific Data Stewardship: design and implement scalable data storage, experiment registration, metadata, provenance, lineage, access control, and findability capabilities. Set the storage, metadata, and stewardship standards that make Integrative Biology omics data trustworthy, reusable, and AI-ready across AWS and GCP. Define Standards and Best Practices: establish and maintain standards, architectural patterns, and governance frameworks for the capability area. Get them documented and adopted by delivery teams and contractors. Collaborate with Capability Lead and Business Stakeholders: work closely with the R&D capability lead to understand business needs, translate scientific requirements into technical solutions, and keep the backlog prioritized. Be the technical partner scientists and product stakeholders can rely on. Lead Contractor Teams and Drive Delivery: direct contractors as needed: provide technical guidance, review their work, and hold the line on quality, scope, and timelines. Provide Technical Guidance and Architecture Leadership: make and document key technical decisions, review designs and implementations, and guide technical direction for contractors and cross-functional partners in the capability area. * Strong Python, C, C++ or Lua skills for analysis, automation and log parsing.
* Deep familiarity with Linux/Unix internals, network monitoring and PCAP analysis.
* Ability to independently verify exploit behavior safely and communicate actionable findings.

**Nice to have**
